architecture: Universal workbook-driven scheduler with protected-tier selection, independent exact-artifact validation, and fail-closed publication
identity_authority: Run identity, engine SHA-256, input snapshot SHA-256, independent validation seal, and package manifest; the compatibility filename tag is not release identity
patch_applied: P-1 memoisation + A-1/A-2/A-3/A-7 input-contract fidelity. Canonical contract hash identical on all 10 workbooks. | Merged L6.3.2.6 coverage-split line; formula audit F-1..F-5; anchor hand-off margin; feasibility-probe retry; starved Stage-1 before-basis profile; interval-averaged break-capacity advisory; joint-search memory guard; blank staffing = current-week only. S2-PAR (parallel Stage-2 break solve) applied on its pre-registered A/B (evidence/s2par_e2e). DNBS day-neighbourhood break search with its own budget phase applied on its pre-registered 3600 s two-seed A/B (evidence/dnbs_e2e_3600b). Joint-solve isolation (joint-refinement CP-SAT solves in a forked, memory-watched child; identical results when memory suffices, a recorded memory stop instead of a killed run when it does not) applied on its registered verification rule (evidence/joint_solve_isolation). Joint refinement and the no-candidate endgame off by default at every depth (474 audits, improved 0; evidence/JOINT_REFINEMENT_REMOVED.md); flags turn them back on. Opt-in only (measured, not shipped): Stage-1 profile rotation for seed portfolios (evidence/profile_diversity_ab) and break-load feedback (evidence/break_load_feedback_ab). Not applied: F-6; LP-visible hit links (measured, no gain). Evidence: evidence/NIGHT_14_TEST_SUITES_AND_BENCHMARKS.md. | Hard-rule conflict report (2026-10-03): a FAIL_HARD_CONTRACT_INFEASIBLE/UNKNOWN outcome names the conflicting rule families in plain words and lists each fixed request that starts outside its associate's enforced language window (fixed_requests_outside_language_windows); findings are printed as readable lines instead of raw solver dumps. Reporting only: the solve path and every schedule are unchanged (evidence/language_hours). | Isolated-solve orphan race (2026-10-03): the forked child arms PR_SET_PDEATHSIG first and then re-checks its parent, so an engine killed between fork() and prctl() no longer leaves its solve running (was 1 in about 40 side-by-side runs of the isolation suite; a 1 s delayed-arming test fails on the old order every time). No schedule change. | Outcome text (2026-10-03): findings print as 'CODE: detail (field=value, ...)'; a production-eligible run labels them 'Warnings', not 'Main blockers'. Text only. | Shift consistency polish (2026-10-03), on by default under its registered rule (evidence/shift_consistency): after selection, same-day shifts are re-dealt among associates of one language and shift length (coverage-identical), and +-1 h moves are kept only when no guarded metric gets worse; every hard rule, fixed request and nesting group is kept, and no employee guard may get worse. 14 cases: 13 more consistent, none worse, validator PASS end to end. | Production-readiness audit Phase A (2026-10-03, evidence/production_readiness_audit): (A1) duplicate populated rows on Preference/Fixed Request are refused and an empty duplicate can no longer erase a populated row; (A2) leave days count against the week: required OFF = min(2 or 3, 7 - leave days), shared by every model, validate_schedule, the independent validator and the clean-room check, plus a contract check naming any associate whose requests cannot fit; (A3) day columns bound by Sun..Sat text or by real calendar dates (weekday), never by position; employee ID bound by header; duplicate, missing or off-grid demand rows, duplicate shrinkage rows, roster rows below a long blank gap, unreadable shift labels, non-integer or negative language minimums and unreadable previous-Saturday shifts are refused; (A4) concurrency metrics published under two names, active-demand quarters (unchanged, what the selector reads) and every staffed quarter (*_all_staffed_quarters), on both engine and validator, both in the parity surface; (A5) the strict release check blocks on gate families in FAIL mode, not on warnings. All 110 workbooks in the repository parse with identical contract results and parsed facts; no search or selection change. | Production-readiness audit Phase B (2026-10-03, evidence/production_readiness_audit/phase_b): (B1, F-05) an overnight language rule with Coverage Days belongs to the day it starts: Mon-Fri 18:00-05:00 is in force Mon 18:00 to Sat 05:00, not Mon 00:00-05:00; (B2, F-08) the contract fingerprint covers the language working window mode and windows, coverage split rules and gate mode, the OFF/leave/preference/fixed switches, 11H mode, the polish setting and every personal request, and run_parameters records the window and polish overrides; (B3, F-12/F-13) Coverage Split rows are read completely or refused (blank Active? included), the Coverage Split Gate Mode is wired into the production quality gate, the independent validator and the clean-room checker recompute Coverage Split shortfalls after breaks (coverage_split_gap_count joins the parity surface, 51 -> 52 fields), and validate_schedule checks hard-OFF and leave preferences, the Sat->Sun and previous-Saturday rest, consecutive OFF, nesting groups and the language window; (B4, F-19) the runner runs the clean-room checker after the validator and blocks on a violation or a metric that disagrees with the engine; (B5, F-10/F-14) a no-schedule run spends its unused budget on the diagnosis; fixed shifts in banned blank hours or outside the language window are refused before solving and named; a diagnostics-only run is reported as one; the engine's diagnosis of a no-schedule run is kept; a blocked schedule lists why; findings are not printed twice; a failed break search claims an exception-cap gap only when the proven minimum exceeds the cap; (B6, F-16) every alternative export is independently validated (the validator now recognises their artifact type); (B7, F-11) every numeric instruction row is checked, contradictions (no-break limit 0, long durations without 11H mode, zero shift variety, the same label twice with different values) are refused, and an Instructions sheet headed Value | Purpose no longer reads its notes as values. All 111 workbooks in the repository parse with identical contract results, parsed facts and language rules in force per quarter; no search or selection change. Phase C of the production-readiness audit: (C1, F-06) when no schedule meets every hard rule - the contract's capacity proofs fail, the hard probe is INFEASIBLE or UNKNOWN, or no break-feasible candidate exists - an elastic pass gives every coverage minimum (nobody on the floor, language, opening, Coverage Split, hard floor, next-Sunday minimums) a reported slack, keeps every person rule hard, and exports a non-releasable HARD_RULE_SHORTFALL_SCHEDULE with a Shortfalls sheet; the runner checks it independently (SHORTFALLS_CONFIRMED) and always exits non-zero; input errors still get no schedule; (C1, F-07) the next-Sunday floor is measured as coverage quality (NEXT_SUNDAY_FLOOR_GAPS), not a hard failure; zero staffing, language and opening on next Sunday stay hard; (F-33) the shortfall pass builds Stage-2 balance terms from fresh expressions (an OR-Tools in-place mutation corrupts the shared ones); normal runs keep the legacy terms because the pre-registered A/B did not pass; (F-34) the Stage-1 window is sized from the configured minimum slice, identical at the default; (C2, F-20) optional 'Break Set For Shifts Of N Hours Or More' rows, read by the engine, the validator and the clean-room checker; (C4, F-28) optional 'Coverage Objective Weighting = Volume Weighted' (default Interval Count, unchanged). Without the new rows, the Stage-1 and Stage-2 models of every packaged and real-run workbook are constraint-for-constraint identical to the Phase B engine, and all 111 repository workbooks parse identically. Phase C4 follow-up: each program chooses its coverage measure. The template builder adds a 'Coverage Objective Weighting' dropdown (Interval Count / Volume Weighted, seeded Interval Count, the empty-cell meaning, so no contract changes), and the engine, the production runner, the Colab runner and both notebooks take a per-run override (--coverage-objective-weighting INTERVAL_COUNT|VOLUME_WEIGHTED; notebook COVERAGE_MEASURE). Run override beats workbook beats default; the override is in the contract fingerprint, and the measure used and its source are in the audit and on the first lines of BUSINESS_OUTCOME.txt. No search change when neither is set. Audit F-35 (found in the C4 impact A/B): the shift-consistency polish replaced the measured schedule but never the published one (no workbook ever carried it), and when it moved a shift by an hour the audit disagreed with the published workbook and the parity gate blocked a valid schedule. Business decision: publish exactly what was published before; the polish is withheld (audit status WITHHELD_PENDING_VALIDATION) until validated on its own, and run_case now refuses to measure one schedule and publish another (recommended_export_pair, PublishedScheduleMismatch). Published schedules are unchanged. F-35 follow-up (business decision): the selected schedule is never rewritten; an applied shift-consistency polish is published beside it as MORE_CONSISTENT_CANDIDATE, written from the polished pair itself, recognised by the independent validator, and approved by the runner only when the validator finds its coverage no worse than the selected schedule's; BUSINESS_OUTCOME.txt then names it with its start-time movement before and after.
